title: Arithmetic Subarrays
summary: An arithmetic sequence consists of at least two elements with a constant difference between consecutive elements.
statement: An arithmetic sequence consists of at least two elements with a constant difference between consecutive elements. Given an array of integers nums and two arrays l and r for range queries, determine if each subarray defined by [l[i], r[i]] can be rearranged into an arithmetic sequence, returning a list of boolean values indicating the result for each query.
constraints: 2–500 numbers and 1–500 inclusive queries; every query has at least two elements.
For each query, return whether its values can be rearranged with one constant adjacent difference.
hints: A multiset is arithmetic exactly when its sorted adjacent differences are all equal.
Sort each queried slice and compare every gap with its first gap.
For each inclusive range, form its sorted values and append the all-equal-gap result.
Sorting gives the only nondecreasing arrangement; any arithmetic rearrangement can be ordered this way with a constant nonnegative gap.
editorial: Sorting gives the only nondecreasing arrangement; any arithmetic rearrangement can be ordered this way with a constant nonnegative gap.

tests.explanation: The first and third sorted subarrays have constant differences; the second does not.
All equal values form an arithmetic sequence with difference zero.
